terms.gloss: here is … for you (handing something over)
evidence: Traupman 113: Ecce tibi decem dollarōs, here are your ten dollars
terms.comment: Classically ecce tibi introduces something new and unexpected, “and look, here comes …” (ecce tibi exortus est Isocratēs, Cic. de Or. 2.22 fin., Lewis & Short s.v. ecce). Handing over money with it is Traupman’s use; Em! or Accipe says it in the comic way.

phrases.latin: «Accipe, em. Ita tenē: laeva ministeriō, dextra est intenta labōrī.»
phrases.english: “Here, take it. Hold it like this: the left hand helps, the right does the work.”
